newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer despite LME stock hikes.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer despite LME stock hikes.

text.p: COMEX copper ended firmer Friday, capping a week of steady gains that recovered ground from last week's selloff despite a big increase in LME stocks.
September COMEX copper settled 0.95 cent firmer at 107.40 cents, traded 108.40 to 105.60 cents. Spot July went out 0.90 cent higher at 109.80 cents.
Although September was able to move marginally over the 108.00 cent mark, further upside progress will hinge on closing above this area of resistance, John Gross of the Copper Journal, said.
"I think we have made a fairly nice recovery on prices in the last couple of days given the dramatic increase in warehouse stocks," Gross added.
LME stocks rose 7,800 tonnes Friday to 181,150 tonnes.
LME stocks have increased sharply this week, up 42,025 tonnes to their highest total since March as the strong LME cash to three months backwardation built inventories.
COMEX stocks have shrunk as metal flowed into LME depots in the U.S. because of an LME premium over COMEX.
Friday, COMEX stocks fell 1,081 short tons to 28,612 tons.
Nevertheless, the backwardation eased by Friday to $140/$150, sharply down from the week's peak of $270.

The easing will allow dealers to worry less about nearby tightness and focus more on the LME three-months price which should begin to reflect a period when the seasonal slowdown will be over and demand re-ignites, analysts said.
